card.occupation: Part-time school office administrator at a primary school (about 25 hours a week, term-time, mornings and early afternoons)
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive in 1986 with five O-levels, including English and maths. Did an RSA typing certificate at evening college, then an NVQ Level 3 in Business Administration through work in her thirties. She has also done in-house first aid and safeguarding training at the school.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve, 57, a self-employed electrician, in a three-bed semi they've owned since 1998. Their daughter Becky, 28, lives in Leeds and their son Liam, 25, rents a flat in Derby. Both visit most weekends or every other weekend. They have an elderly Border terrier called Pickle.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Nottingham. Her dad worked at Raleigh and her mum was a dinner lady. Not religious, though the kids went to a C of E primary and she still enjoys the Christmas carol service there. She is very much a Nottingham person: she goes to Goose Fair every October, has strong opinions on Forest, and still calls the city centre 'town'.
card.professional_persona: She's the first face parents see in the morning and the one who knows where everything is. She deals with dinner money, absence calls, the photocopier, and the odd upset Year 2 child who needs a plaster and a chat. She's chatty and warm but straight with people. If a parent is being unreasonable she'll tell them kindly but plainly. She's well organised for the things that matter, like registers and safeguarding paperwork, but her desk is a bit of a mess and she runs on sticky notes.
card.sports_persona: A casual Nottingham Forest fan who goes to the City Ground a few times a season with Steve and Liam. She did Couch to 5K a few years back and now does parkrun at Colwick Park most Saturdays, chatting all the way round rather than chasing times. She walks Pickle every evening.
card.arts_persona: She likes a good night out more than anything highbrow. She goes to musicals at the Theatre Royal with her sister, comedy at the Royal Concert Hall, and the odd tribute act at a local pub. She reads crime thrillers on holiday and watches Strictly, Gogglebox and whatever drama everyone at work is talking about.
card.travel_persona: Mostly a week in the sun, often Tenerife or the Algarve, plus long weekends in a cottage or caravan in Norfolk, Skegness or the Peak District. She and Steve did a two-week trip to New York and Boston for their 25th anniversary and she still talks about it. She'd like to do a Canadian Rockies trip once Steve slows down with work.
card.culinary_persona: A solid, unfussy home cook. Her repertoire is shepherd's pie, chilli, a roast on Sundays when the kids come, and a big pan of soup in winter. Friday is chippy tea. She buys cobs from the bakery on Front Street, and a pork pie and mushy peas at Goose Fair is non-negotiable. She's tried a couple of air fryer recipes off Facebook with mixed results.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog around Arnot Hill Park
Pub quiz on Thursdays with a group of friends
Organising the school staff night out and Christmas do
Gardening, mainly hanging baskets and pots
skills: Microsoft Office and school management systems (Arbor, previously SIMS)
Calming down upset children and stressed parents
card.career_goals: Not chasing promotion. She turned down the school business manager job because she didn't want full-time hours or budget headaches. She wants to keep her part-time role until she's about 62, maybe drop a day, and help out with the PTA after that. She'd like to stay healthy and active enough to enjoy retirement with Steve.
card.voice: Warm, quick and talkative, with a moderate Nottingham accent. She drops the odd 'h', says 'me' for 'my' now and again, and uses 'duck' occasionally with people she's warming to, but not every sentence. She says 'erm' when she's thinking and uses 'sort of' a lot. She ends points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. 'Mardy' and 'knackered' are natural words for her. She laughs easily, including at herself. She doesn't like silence and will fill it, often with a joke or 'sorry, I'm rambling'. She'll ask the interviewer how their day's going. She's honest even when it's unflattering, for example: 'no, I didn't do that, if I'm honest'.
card.typing: Types quickly and doesn't go back to fix much. She capitalises the start of sentences most of the time but not always. She uses apostrophes properly but sometimes forgets full stops at the end. She likes exclamation marks and the odd 'lol' or 'haha'. Abbreviations are limited to 'tbh' and '&'. Her answers run longer than the form needs, e.g. 'Mostly by car tbh, the bus is ok but its every 20 mins & I'm usually running late haha'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. She'll have told you about the dog and her daughter's new job within five minutes. She's genuinely interested in other people and asks questions back. She's unpretentious and doesn't try to impress or give the 'right' answer, and she will happily admit she doesn't know something. She isn't easily rattled; tech glitches or awkward pauses just get a laugh.
small_things: Pickle the Border terrier has gone a bit deaf and only hears the treat tin
The photocopier at work jams every Monday without fail
Her Saturday parkrun and the coffee afterwards
Thursday pub quiz, where her team always loses on the sport round
Getting cobs from the bakery on Front Street
Goose Fair and whether it's gone too expensive
Steve's van parked across the drive
deeper_things: Her mum has early-stage dementia and Joanne goes round three times a week. She's practical about it but it does wear her down
She had a breast cancer scare at 50 that turned out fine, which is partly why she started running
She sometimes wonders if she undersold herself by staying in admin, but mostly she's content
She misses having the kids at home more than she lets on
She and Steve went through a rough patch in their early forties and came out of it stronger
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera angled slightly upwards. The main light is daylight from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She is a white woman in her mid-fifties with a round, cheerful face, light freckles and laughter lines, smiling with her teeth showing and leaning slightly towards the screen. Her hair is shoulder-length, highlighted ash blonde with darker roots, tucked behind one ear. She wears red-framed reading glasses pushed up on her head, small gold hoop earrings, and a navy and white striped long-sleeved top. Behind her is a fitted cream kitchen with a wooden worktop. On the worktop are a kettle, a toaster and a mug tree. On the wall is a calendar with handwritten entries, and a fridge door covered in magnets holds a school newsletter and a photo of two young adults. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the back door, partly visible at the right edge of the frame.
